context.current_question: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Technology Associate Certificate. Is it available to international applicants?
So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?

definitions.E4:
No. The Civil Technology Associate Certificate is **not available to international applicants**. International applicants interested in civil technology are directed to consider the **Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering**.

[View the Civil Technology program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.
definitions.E5:
No. The program’s international restriction means you **cannot be admitted to the Civil Technology Associate Certificate as an international applicant**. It does not indicate automatic admission to another program, including the Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering; that would require a separate admissions assessment.

[View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/)
definitions.E1:
**I can verify:**

- Civil Technology is an active, part-time Associate Certificate delivered in a blended format at Burnaby and online.
- The credential requires at least **30 credits**, including **at least 9.5 credits from the approved elective pool**.
- The curriculum includes courses such as **CIVL 1120 — Statics**, **CIVL 1121 — Graphical Communication**, and **CIVL 1160 — Applied Hydrology**, plus approved electives.
- English proficiency is listed as **Category 3—English Studies 12 at 50% or equivalent**. Math 12 or **MATH 0001 — Technical Mathematics** is recommended for success.

**Confirm directly with BCIT:**

- The revised curriculum, because the program is under review.
- Whether your prior education satisfies any “equivalent” prerequisite.
- Current course availability and whether departmental approval is required.
- Admission requirements for any different program you may pursue.

See the [Civil Technology program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/) or contact the program assistant for the curriculum review details.
definitions.E6: Note: This program is under review, and a curriculum change is planned. For more information, please contact the Program Assistant . Please note that this program is not available to international applicants. International applicants interested in civil technology are encouraged to view the BCIT Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering . Delivery: blended. See details . The Part-time Associate Certificate in Civil Technology is designed to provide students and employers a flexible offering of academic courses to advance careers in the field of Civil Technology. A program of study can be tailored to a student’s needs by selecting appropriate courses from the list of electives. An Associate Certificate must contain a minimum of 30.0 credits and approved courses from the Associate Certificate can be incorporated into the requirements for a Certificate . All Program Declarations must be submitted for approval by the Civil Engineering department. Notice: Please be advised that the program is currently under review and will undergo a curriculum change. Next up Entrance Requirements
definitions.E7: Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. Program location Courses may be offered at the following locations: Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Distance and online learning Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs
definitions.E2: How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing.
